best_for: Music collectors with a large local library who liked Amarok 1.4 and want a free player that also handles podcasts, internet radio, tag fixes and copying music to old players.

points.title: Built around your own files
points.text: It organizes a local library with smart and dynamic playlists, CUE sheets, audio CDs and a tag editor that can fetch tags from MusicBrainz. Missing covers come from Last.fm, MusicBrainz or Discogs.

points.title: Streams and cloud folders too
points.text: It plays internet radio such as SomaFM, Digitally Imported and Jamendo, and music stored on Subsonic, Plex, Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, Box or Seafile. Spotify is not on the list.

points.title: Converts and copies to devices
points.text: You can transcode to MP3, Ogg Vorbis, Opus, FLAC, AAC, WMA or WAV and copy music to an iPod, MTP or USB player. Podcasts sync through gpodder.net.

points.title: Remote control from Android
points.text: The Clementine Remote app on Google Play controls playback from your phone. MPRIS, a Wii Remote and the command line work as well.

points.title: Windows lags behind
points.text: The project announced 1.4.6 for all three systems, but the Windows listing here has 2 versions and stops at 1.4.1, a 32-bit installer. macOS and Linux list only 1.4.6, so older builds there need another source.

points.title: Mac build is for new Apple silicon
points.text: The macOS download here is an Arm64 disk image that needs macOS 15 or later, so Intel Macs and older systems are left out.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is a community package
points.text: The Flathub build covers x64 and Arm64, but Flathub marks it unverified: it is not published or supported by the Clementine developers.

points.title: Frequent test builds
points.text: Development builds land on GitHub as pre-releases, often several a day, if you want a fix before the next stable release. They are not the stable line.
